lessons.title: Use two key words
lessons.strategy: Some questions have two key words, such as a person and a day. The answer is in the sentence that fits both, not just one.
lessons.tip: Underline the two key words in the question before you look.

worked.prompt: What did Uncle Selvam do on Sunday?
worked.answer: He fixed a wooden seat to the swing.
steps: The question has two key words: Uncle Selvam and Sunday.
Uncle Selvam did something on Saturday too: he tied the rope swing. That sentence fits only one key word.
Find the sentence with Sunday: 'On Sunday, he fixed a wooden seat to it.' Both key words fit, so that is the answer.

lessons.title: Before and after
lessons.strategy: A question may ask what happened just before or just after something. Find that event in the text first, then read the sentence in front of it or behind it.
lessons.tip: Put your finger on the event the question names, then move one sentence.

worked.prompt: What happened just before Uncle Selvam tied a stronger knot?
worked.answer: Meena shouted and held the swing.
steps: Find the event in the question: 'Uncle Selvam tied a stronger knot.'
The question says before, so read the sentence in front of it: Meena shouted, 'Stop!' and held the swing with both hands.
Check the order: the rope slipped, Meena held the swing, then came the knot. So the answer is that Meena shouted and held the swing.

lessons.title: So points back to the reason
lessons.strategy: The word so joins a reason to what happened. The part before so is the reason. The part after so is the result.
lessons.tip: Find so, then read the words in front of it.

worked.prompt: Why did Meena let Arul go first?
steps: Find the sentence: 'her little brother Arul was crying, so she let him go first.'
The word so joins two parts. Before so is the reason; after so is what happened.
Before so: Arul was crying. That is why she let him go first.

lessons.title: What they say and what they do
lessons.strategy: To find a feeling, put two clues together: the words a person says, and what the person does at that moment.
lessons.tip: Ask: when would I say that and do that?

worked.prompt: How did Meena feel when the rope began to slip?
worked.answer: She was frightened that Arul would fall.
steps: Look at what Meena said: she shouted, 'Stop!' People shout like that when something is going wrong.
Look at what she did: she held the swing with both hands, to keep it still.
Put the two together: she was frightened that Arul would fall.

lessons.title: Pick the best title
lessons.strategy: A good title fits the whole text. A title that fits only one sentence is a detail, not the main idea.
lessons.tip: Try each title against the first paragraph, then against the second.

worked.prompt: Which is the best title: 'A New Swing', 'Lunch Time' or 'Arul Cries'?
steps: A good title fits the whole text, not just one part.
'Lunch Time' fits only two words, and 'Arul Cries' fits only one sentence.
Every part is about the swing: making it, sharing it and mending it. So 'A New Swing' is the best title.

lessons.title: How could you check it?
lessons.strategy: For a fact, you can say how to check it: look, count, measure or ask someone who was there. If there is no way to check, it is an opinion.
lessons.tip: Finish this sentence: I could check it by ...

worked.prompt: Is this a fact or an opinion: 'A swing is the best toy in the world.'?
steps: Ask: how could I check it? For 'On Sunday, he fixed a wooden seat to it', you could look at the swing or ask Uncle Selvam.
For 'the best toy in the world' there is nothing to count, measure or look at. Some children would choose a ball or a kite.
If you cannot say how to check it, it is an opinion.

passages.title: The Mango Tree Swing
passages.text:
Uncle Selvam tied a rope swing to the mango tree on Saturday. On Sunday, he fixed a wooden seat to it. Meena wanted the first turn, but her little brother Arul was crying, so she let him go first. Arul laughed as he flew up.

After lunch, Arul was on the swing again. The rope began to slip. Meena shouted, “Stop!” and held the swing with both hands. Uncle Selvam tied a stronger knot. Then Meena had her turn at last. She said, “I knew it would be worth the wait.” A swing is the best toy in the world.

passages.title: The Kite Shop
passages.text:
On Friday, Bala went to the kite shop with his father. He chose a green kite with a long tail. On Saturday, he came back with his sister Devi, and she chose a red one. The shopkeeper gave each of them a free reel of string.

On Sunday the wind was weak, so the kites would not rise. Devi stamped her foot and said, “This is not fair!” Then a strong wind came from the sea. Both kites climbed high above the houses. Flying a kite is the most exciting game of all.

questions.prompt: Who chose a kite on Saturday?
questions.evidence: On Saturday, he came back with his sister Devi, and she chose a red one.
questions.explain: Two children chose kites. Bala chose his on Friday. The sentence with Saturday says that his sister chose a red one.
questions.hint: Two days are named. Find the sentence with Saturday in it.

questions.prompt: What happened just after Devi stamped her foot?
questions.right: A strong wind came from the sea.
questions.evidence: Then a strong wind came from the sea.
questions.explain: Find where Devi stamped her foot. The next sentence begins with Then: a strong wind came from the sea.
questions.hint: Find the sentence about her foot, then read the one that follows it.

questions.prompt: Why would the kites not rise on Sunday?
questions.evidence: On Sunday the wind was weak, so the kites would not rise.
questions.explain: The part before so is the reason: the wind was weak.
questions.hint: Find the word so. The reason is the part in front of it.

questions.prompt: How did Devi feel when the kites would not rise?
questions.evidence: Devi stamped her foot and said
questions.explain: She stamped her foot and said, “This is not fair!” People do and say that when they are cross.
questions.hint: Look at what she did with her foot and at what she said.

questions.prompt: Which is the best title for this text?
questions.evidence: Both kites climbed high above the houses.
questions.explain: Every part is about the two kites: buying them, waiting for wind and flying them. The string and the sea wind are each in one sentence only.
questions.hint: Which title fits the first paragraph and the second one too?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Flying a kite is the most exciting game of all.
wrong: He chose a green kite with a long tail.
Then a strong wind came from the sea.
questions.evidence: Flying a kite is the most exciting game of all.
questions.explain: Nobody can check which game is the most exciting; other children may choose a different one. You could check the colour of the kite and the wind.
questions.hint: For each sentence, ask how you could check it. One of them has nothing to look at or count.

passages.title: The Clock That Stopped
passages.text:
The big clock in the school hall stopped on Monday. On Tuesday, the bell rang ten minutes late. On Wednesday it rang twenty minutes early. The cook did not know when to serve lunch, so the rice went cold.

Mr Pillai, the science teacher, opened the clock on Thursday. He found a dead battery inside. Before he put in a new one, he let Class Five look at the tiny wheels. Rani clapped her hands and said, “It is like a little machine city!” Now the bell rings on time. Old clocks are more beautiful than new ones.

questions.prompt: On which day did the bell ring early?
questions.evidence: On Wednesday it rang twenty minutes early
questions.explain: The bell rang at the wrong time on two days. Tuesday goes with late; Wednesday goes with early.
questions.hint: Two days are about the bell. Match the day to the word early.

questions.prompt: What did Mr Pillai do before he put in a new battery?
questions.right: He let Class Five look at the wheels.
wrong: He rang the bell on time.
questions.evidence: Before he put in a new one, he let Class Five look at the tiny wheels.
questions.explain: The sentence begins with Before: before the new battery went in, he let Class Five look at the tiny wheels.
questions.hint: Find the sentence that begins with Before. Its second part happened first.

questions.prompt: Why did the rice go cold?
questions.right: The cook did not know when to serve lunch.
wrong: The children came late on purpose.
questions.evidence: The cook did not know when to serve lunch, so the rice went cold.
questions.explain: The part before so is the reason: the cook did not know when to serve lunch.
questions.hint: Find the word so. Read the part in front of it.

questions.prompt: How did Rani feel when she saw inside the clock?
questions.evidence: Rani clapped her hands and said
questions.explain: She clapped her hands and said it was like a little machine city. People clap and talk like that when they are delighted.
questions.hint: What did she do with her hands? What did she say?

questions.prompt: Which is the best title for this text?
questions.evidence: The big clock in the school hall stopped on Monday.
questions.explain: Each part is about the clock: it stops, the bell goes wrong and the teacher mends it. The rice and Rani's clapping are single details.
questions.hint: Which title covers both the trouble and the mending?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Old clocks are more beautiful than new ones.
wrong: He found a dead battery inside.
Now the bell rings on time.
questions.evidence: Old clocks are more beautiful than new ones.
questions.explain: Nobody can measure which clocks are more beautiful. You could look at the battery and listen for the bell.
questions.hint: Which sentence could you not check by looking, counting or listening?

passages.title: The New Bus Stop
passages.text:
For years, the children of Pudur waited for the school bus under the hot sun. In March, the village built a small shelter with a tin roof. In April, the carpenter added a long bench.

One morning it rained hard. Kumar reached the stop late, so he had no seat. A small girl moved her bag and said, “Sit here, please.” Kumar smiled and shared his biscuits with her. After the rain stopped, the bus arrived, dry and shining. Our bus stop is the nicest place in the village.

questions.prompt: What was added in April?
questions.evidence: In April, the carpenter added a long bench.
questions.explain: Two months are named. March goes with the shelter and its tin roof; April goes with the bench.

questions.prompt: What happened after the rain stopped?
questions.evidence: After the rain stopped, the bus arrived
questions.explain: The sentence begins with After the rain stopped, and goes on: the bus arrived.

questions.prompt: Why did Kumar have no seat?
questions.evidence: Kumar reached the stop late, so he had no seat.
questions.explain: The part before so is the reason: he reached the stop late.

questions.prompt: How did Kumar feel when the girl made room for him?
questions.evidence: Kumar smiled and shared his biscuits with her.
questions.explain: He smiled and shared his biscuits with her. People do that when they are thankful.

questions.prompt: Which is the best title for this text?
questions.right: A Shelter at the Bus Stop
questions.evidence: the village built a small shelter with a tin roof
questions.explain: Both paragraphs are about the shelter: how it was built and how it helped in the rain. The biscuits are one detail, and the rain is only in the second paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Our bus stop is the nicest place in the village.
wrong: In April, the carpenter added a long bench.
questions.evidence: Our bus stop is the nicest place in the village.
questions.explain: You cannot check which place is the nicest; people will not agree. You could look at the bench and ask about the rain.

passages.title: The Calf's First Day
passages.text:
Lakshmi's cow had a calf on Tuesday night. On Wednesday morning, Lakshmi carried warm water to the shed. In the evening, her brother Mani brought fresh grass. The calf was too weak to stand, so Lakshmi held the bottle for it.

Before she went to bed, Lakshmi looked into the shed one more time. The calf was standing on its thin legs. She ran to the house and called, “Come and see, come and see!” Her grandmother named the calf Chandra. A calf is the sweetest animal on a farm.

questions.prompt: Who brought fresh grass in the evening?
questions.evidence: In the evening, her brother Mani brought fresh grass.
questions.explain: Two children brought things. Lakshmi brought water in the morning; Mani brought grass in the evening.

questions.prompt: What did Lakshmi do before she went to bed?
questions.right: She looked into the shed again.
wrong: She carried warm water to the shed.
questions.evidence: Before she went to bed, Lakshmi looked into the shed one more time.
questions.explain: The sentence begins with Before she went to bed: she looked into the shed one more time. The water was carried in the morning, and it was Grandmother who named the calf.

questions.prompt: Why did Lakshmi hold the bottle for the calf?
questions.right: The calf was too weak to stand.
wrong: The calf did not like grass.
questions.evidence: The calf was too weak to stand, so Lakshmi held the bottle for it.
questions.explain: The part before so is the reason: the calf was too weak to stand.

questions.prompt: How did Lakshmi feel when she saw the calf standing?
questions.evidence: She ran to the house and called
questions.explain: She ran and called, “Come and see, come and see!” People run and call out like that when they are excited.

questions.prompt: Which is the best title for this text?
questions.evidence: The calf was standing on its thin legs.
questions.explain: The whole text follows the calf through its first day, from weak to standing. Mani's grass is one detail, and the farm itself is not described.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: A calf is the sweetest animal on a farm.
wrong: Her grandmother named the calf Chandra.
The calf was standing on its thin legs.
questions.evidence: A calf is the sweetest animal on a farm.
questions.explain: There is no way to check which animal is the sweetest. You could ask about the name and look at the calf.

passages.title: The Painted Wall
passages.text:
The wall behind the library was grey and dirty. In June, Class Four painted a river along the lower half. In July, Class Five painted birds and clouds at the top. The art teacher, Miss Thomas, drew the outlines with chalk first.

On the last day, a football hit the wet paint, so one cloud got a brown mark. Anil hung his head and said, “I am so sorry, Miss.” Miss Thomas turned the mark into a flying kite. After that, every child signed the corner of the wall. Painted walls are much prettier than plain ones.

questions.prompt: What did Class Five paint?
questions.evidence: In July, Class Five painted birds and clouds at the top.
questions.explain: Two classes painted. Class Four painted the river; Class Five painted birds and clouds.

questions.prompt: What happened after Miss Thomas turned the mark into a kite?
wrong: A football hit the wet paint.
questions.evidence: After that, every child signed the corner of the wall.
questions.explain: The next sentence begins with After that: every child signed the corner of the wall.

questions.prompt: Why did one cloud get a brown mark?
questions.right: A football hit the wet paint.
questions.evidence: a football hit the wet paint, so one cloud got a brown mark
questions.explain: The part before so is the reason: a football hit the wet paint.

questions.prompt: How did Anil feel about the mark?
questions.evidence: Anil hung his head and said
questions.explain: He hung his head and said he was so sorry. People do that when they feel ashamed of something.

questions.prompt: Which is the best title for this text?
questions.evidence: Class Four painted a river along the lower half
questions.explain: Every part is about the wall turning into a picture. The football and the chalk are each in one sentence only.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Painted walls are much prettier than plain ones.
wrong: In June, Class Four painted a river along the lower half.
Miss Thomas turned the mark into a flying kite.
questions.evidence: Painted walls are much prettier than plain ones.
questions.explain: Nobody can measure which walls are prettier. You could look at the river and the kite on the wall.

passages.title: The Lost Puppy
passages.text:
On Monday evening, Fatima found a brown puppy near the bus stand. It had no collar. She gave it milk. Her mother gave it an old towel to sleep on. On Tuesday, Fatima made a poster with a drawing of the puppy.

On Wednesday, an old man knocked at the door. The puppy jumped up and licked his hands, so everyone knew it was his. Fatima bit her lip and said quietly, “Goodbye, little one.” Before he left, the old man asked her to visit every Sunday. Puppies are better pets than kittens.

questions.prompt: What did Fatima's mother give the puppy?
questions.evidence: Her mother gave it an old towel to sleep on
questions.explain: Two people gave the puppy something. Fatima gave milk; her mother gave an old towel.

questions.prompt: What did the old man do before he left?
questions.right: He asked Fatima to visit every Sunday.
wrong: He made a poster of the puppy.
He gave the puppy some milk.
questions.evidence: Before he left, the old man asked her to visit every Sunday.
questions.explain: The sentence begins with Before he left: he asked her to visit every Sunday.

questions.prompt: Why was everyone sure the puppy was the old man's?
questions.right: It jumped up and licked his hands.
wrong: It had his name on its collar.
questions.evidence: The puppy jumped up and licked his hands, so everyone knew it was his.
questions.explain: The part before so is the reason: the puppy jumped up and licked his hands.

questions.prompt: How did Fatima feel when the puppy left?
questions.evidence: Fatima bit her lip and said quietly
questions.explain: She bit her lip and said goodbye quietly. People do that when they are sad and trying not to cry.

questions.prompt: Which is the best title for this text?
questions.evidence: everyone knew it was his
questions.explain: The text follows the puppy from being found to going home with its owner. The poster and the towel are single details.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
questions.right: Puppies are better pets than kittens.
wrong: On Wednesday, an old man knocked at the door.
questions.evidence: Puppies are better pets than kittens.
questions.explain: People who love kittens would not agree, and there is no way to check it. You could look for a collar and ask who came to the door.
